about: How a proto-language draws its inventory from sounds.json: size classes, series, the sounds every language has, and implications. The steps are in README.md.
sources: WALS 1A Consonant Inventories (Maddieson): 563 languages; small 6-14: 89, moderately small 15-18: 122, average 19-25: 201, moderately large 26-33: 94, large 34+: 57.
WALS 2A Vowel Quality Inventories (Maddieson): 564 languages; small 2-4: 93, average 5-6: 288, large 7-14: 183.

WALS 4A Voicing in Plosives and Fricatives; 5A Voicing and Gaps in Plosive Systems; 6A Uvular Consonants; 7A Glottalized Consonants; 8A Lateral Consonants; 10A Vowel Nasalization; 11A Front Rounded Vowels; 13A Tone; 14A Fixed Stress Locations (Goedemans & van der Hulst). Counts rounded to weights.
Implications: Maddieson, I. 1984. Patterns of Sounds. Cambridge University Press; Greenberg, J. 1966. Language Universals.
vowelCountNote: The count is of vowel qualities (short, oral). Long and nasal vowels come from the series below and do not count.

series.note: WALS 4A/5A: about 60 % of languages have a voicing contrast in plosives.
WALS 4A: a voicing contrast in fricatives, mostly together with one in plosives.
Each long vowel needs its short vowel.

seriesNote: A series that is not drawn removes its sounds from the draw. A series that is drawn makes its sounds candidates with their weight from sounds.json; the count classes above still limit the total.

always.note: Each inner list is a choice: the inventory takes at least one of its members. Every language has a nasal, two or more stops, a close front vowel, an open vowel and a back rounded vowel (the 'vowel triangle').

implications.then: the voiceless stop at the same place
the voiceless fricative at the same place
the plain stop at the same place
the plain stop at the same place
the plain stop at the same place
the short vowel of the same quality
the oral vowel of the same quality
the unrounded front vowel of the same height
the fricative or the stop at the same place

implications.note: WALS 5A: a missing /g/ is a common gap; a lone /g/ is rare.

implications.then: p or a gap at p
implications.note: WALS 5A: a missing /p/ is the other common gap (Arabic-type).

implicationNote: strength is the chance that the rule holds. 'needs' is 'then' for a program: a list of choices, each a sound id or a feature replacement on the drawn sound (the notation of changes.json); one of them must be in the inventory. A sound that a gap removed counts as there ('p or a gap at p'). When a drawn sound breaks a rule that holds, the missing sound is added; if the count class is then full, the drawn sound is put back instead.

gaps.note: WALS 5A: missing /g/ in a voiced series.

liquids.note: WALS 8A: 95 of 567 languages have no lateral.

stress.note: No fixed place. The proto-language draws a place per root and keeps it.

stressNote: WALS 14A, rounded. Stress is not shown in a spelling. Changes in changes.json use it ([+stress], [-stress]). Tone (WALS 13A) is not in the kit.
